title: Choose Run It Back's structural direction
question: All three options honor Broadcast Tactical. Choose the composition that should govern the complete draft-to-recap experience.

options.label: Live Results Desk
options.lineage: sports wire results pages and live broadcast rundowns
options.thesis: Every choice is the next live cue in a four-round tournament rundown.
options.viewport: A large premise and Daily action own the left field while a compact match-notes rail explains the five-pick, one-IGL, four-series run.
options.risk: Purposeful density can become noise unless each screen keeps one primary action.

raised.raise: Number every pick and round with strict, learnable identifiers.
Make the highlight feed a legible live transcript with explicit pacing controls.
Keep a visible, exact backtrail at every reversible draft step.

options.label: Broadcast Control Room
options.lineage: production switchers, multiview monitors, and cue sheets
options.thesis: The player directs the broadcast by locking one clear input at a time.
options.viewport: Daily and Free Play read as two program sources beneath a dominant live preview that demonstrates the full run.
options.risk: The most familiar esports-operational option can drift toward a generic dashboard.

options.label: Roster Catalog 05
options.lineage: Factory-style record catalogs fused with event-card collecting
options.thesis: Every player-year card becomes a numbered artifact in one severe tournament catalog.
options.viewport: A disciplined five-slot catalog index surrounds a single active Daily entry and its next action.
options.case: It strongly serves collectors and gives cards identity, but coded navigation needs more explanation than the live desk.
options.risk: Too much code language can hide roles and consequences from first-time players.

options.label: Elbow Panel Console
options.thesis: Thick elbows route each selection into the next stage.
options.viewport: A routed stage path wraps around the active choice.
options.case: Clear routing, but the panel metaphor identifies science fiction before fantasy esports.
options.kept: A continuous stage rail should make the four-round route unmistakable.
options.risk: The console vocabulary can become decorative HUD clutter.

options.label: Deployable Match Sheet
options.thesis: The run unfolds from one pick into a complete bracket.
options.viewport: A compact five-cell draft sheet opens into four tournament cells.
options.case: Excellent progressive disclosure, but the folding geometry adds interaction cost without improving player decisions.
options.kept: Reveal complexity only as the player commits each step.
options.risk: Diagonal geometry harms reflow and reading order.

options.label: Matchday Stack
options.thesis: Each decision is one complete card with an exact return path.
options.viewport: One large Daily card links directly into a strict stack of draft and tournament screens.
options.case: The sequence is clear, but the nostalgic card stack weakens roster comparison and tournament scale.
options.kept: Every reversible decision gets a literal, predictable Back action.
options.risk: Fixed-card proportions do not serve dense desktop comparison or 390px reflow equally.

canonCard.label: Standard dark card dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional responsive game dashboard executed with clean cards and familiar navigation.
canonCard.viewport: A centered hero, two equal mode cards, and a row of feature explanations.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but category-interchangeable and weaker at expressing tournament suspense.
